figures.caption: Fig. 3: t-SNE visualization of label embeddings during the diffusion reverse process on the APTOS 2019 test set. As t decreases from 100 to 0, class clusters become progressively more compact and separable, demonstrating that the semantic-conditioned denoising process effectively reduces prediction uncertainty across DR severity grades.

Fig. 2: Class Activation Map (CAM) visualization on representative APTOS 2019 test samples across five DR severity grades. Row 1: original fundus images. Row 2: activation heatmaps from our LoRA fine-tuned guidance model (with cross-modal semantic conditioning). Row 3: activation heatmaps from the pretrained guidance model (without fine-tuning). The semantically conditioned model produces significantly more focused activations aligned with clinically relevant lesion regions, demonstrating that cross-modal semantic guidance steers the visual encoder toward pathology-aware feature extraction that pure visual supervision cannot achieve.

Fig. 1: Overview of the proposed CGSD framework with two decoupled training stages. Stage 1 (Guidance Adaptation): A frozen Text Encoder and a LoRA-adapted Image Encoder extract ℓ2-normalized text features T and image features f ; their dot product yields the cross-modal semantic vector d ∈ RK . After convergence, all guidance module parameters are frozen. Stage 2 (Diffusion Training): The ground-truth label y0 is progressively noised to yt and concatenated with d as input to the trainable Denoising U-Net ϵθ, optimized by Lϵ. During inference, starting from yT ∼ N (ŷ0, I), the reverse denoising chain produces the final DR grade prediction via softmax.
